title: Round trip through a file
description:
Write `roundtrip(text, length, buffer)`:

1. Create or empty the file `xenon_roundtrip.tmp` (open with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC`, mode `0o644`).
2. Write the `length` bytes at `text` into it, looping until all of them are written.
3. Close it, open it again read-only, and read it into `buffer`, looping until `read` returns 0. Then add a terminating zero byte after the data.
4. Close it and delete it with `unlink`.
5. Return the number of bytes read, or the negative error number of the first call that failed.

The tests check that `rbx`, `rbp` and `r12` to `r15` are unchanged afterwards, so save the ones you use.

solution.solution.asm:
section .data
rt_path: db     "xenon_roundtrip.tmp", 0
        section .text

roundtrip:
        push    rbx                     ; fd
        push    r12                     ; text, then buffer
        push    r13                     ; length, then bytes read
        push    r14                     ; the buffer
        sub     rsp, 8                  ; keep rsp aligned
        mov     r12, rdi
        mov     r13, rsi
        mov     r14, rdx

        mov     eax, 2
        lea     rdi, [rel rt_path]
        mov     esi, 0x241
        mov     edx, 0o644
        syscall
        test    rax, rax
        js      .out
        mov     rbx, rax

.write: test    r13, r13
        jz      .written
        mov     eax, 1
        mov     rdi, rbx
        mov     rsi, r12
        mov     rdx, r13
        syscall
        test    rax, rax
        js      .close_fail
        add     r12, rax
        sub     r13, rax
        jmp     .write
.written:
        mov     eax, 3
        mov     rdi, rbx
        syscall

        mov     eax, 2
        lea     rdi, [rel rt_path]
        xor     esi, esi
        syscall
        test    rax, rax
        js      .out
        mov     rbx, rax
        xor     r13d, r13d              ; bytes read so far
.read:  xor     eax, eax
        mov     rdi, rbx
        lea     rsi, [r14 + r13]
        mov     edx, 4096
        syscall
        test    rax, rax
        js      .close_fail
        jz      .eof
        add     r13, rax
        jmp     .read
.eof:   mov     byte [r14 + r13], 0
        mov     eax, 3
        mov     rdi, rbx
        syscall
        mov     eax, 87
        lea     rdi, [rel rt_path]
        syscall
        mov     rax, r13
        jmp     .out

.close_fail:
        mov     r13, rax                ; keep the error
        mov     eax, 3
        mov     rdi, rbx
        syscall
        mov     rax, r13
.out:   add     rsp, 8
        pop     r14
        pop     r13
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

hints: Keep everything you need after a `syscall` in callee-saved registers (`rbx`, `r12` to `r14`), saved on entry and restored on every way out. `syscall` itself changes `rcx` and `r11`.
Both loops follow the same idea: call, stop on a negative result, otherwise move the pointer on by the number of bytes and go again. For reading, `rax` = 0 means the end of the file.
unitTests:
test "a round trip"
    roundtrip("hello, file", 11, @buf(64)) == 11
    roundtrip("hello, file", 11, @buf(64)) => "hello, file"
    roundtrip("abc", 3, @buf(16)) => "abc"
test "nothing to write"
    roundtrip("", 0, @buf(8)) == 0
    roundtrip("", 0, @buf(8)) => ""

grading.unitTests:
test "a round trip"
    roundtrip("hello, file", 11, @buf(64)) == 11
    roundtrip("hello, file", 11, @buf(64)) => "hello, file"
    roundtrip("abc", 3, @buf(16)) => "abc"
test "nothing to write"
    roundtrip("", 0, @buf(8)) == 0
    roundtrip("", 0, @buf(8)) => ""
